report.summary: Incident S08 covers a P1 alert for payment-service error rate rising to about 22% from roughly 11:00 UTC, with checkout-service errors stepping up at the same time. The system determination is INCONCLUSIVE because the leading hypothesis (H-A, deploy C09 causing payment write failures) reached only 0.45 confidence, below the 0.50 threshold, and its mechanism is unverified. The only change in the window is deploy C09 (v3.2.0) at 10:57:00Z, about three minutes before onset, but schema migration status is unrecorded and no payment-service error logs could be retrieved. Resource metrics and traffic were flat at onset, and downstream health checks were shallow and taken at 11:28Z. A provider or issuer decline spike (H-B, 0.25) cannot be excluded because provider telemetry is absent and one checkout log cites a card declined by issuer. The cause is therefore unconfirmed, and the checks listed in open_questions are needed to settle it.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: Deploy C09 (v3.2.0) at 10:57:00Z added idempotency_key writes and upgraded the ORM 5.x to 6.x; if the schema migration was not applied before the new code served writes, payment writes fail, producing the step to about 21% error rate in the 11:00 bucket. Checkout 5xx would propagate via the sync_http edge D04.

brief.title: payment-service errors
brief.alert: ALERT [P1] payment-service error rate 22% since ~11:00 UTC; payments failing.

plan.incident_understanding: payment-service error rate rose to about 22% starting around 11:00 UTC, with checkout-service also alerting, so payment failures are propagating into checkout. Telemetry covers 10:00 to 11:30 UTC. The cause is not yet known; it could be a recent deployment or config change to payment-service, a failing downstream dependency (e.g. a payment provider, database or fraud/auth service), a shared infrastructure event, or a traffic or capacity problem.
candidate_explanations: A deployment or config/feature-flag change to payment-service around 11:00 UTC introduced a regression causing errors
A downstream dependency of payment-service (external payment provider, database, or internal service) degraded around 11:00 UTC and payment-service errors propagate
An infrastructure event or capacity saturation (CPU, connection pool, rate limit) in payment-service or its hosts started around 11:00 UTC
A dependency change in checkout-service (e.g. a new call to payment-service or changed timeout/retry behaviour) is amplifying or causing the failures

critique.summary: The leading hypothesis H-A (C09 deploy) is plausible given timing and P02, but the analysis overstates support: the only direct error evidence is a card-decline log that points at issuer-side declines, payment-service error logs were never retrieved, and the schema migration timing is unknown. H-B is dismissed too quickly on the basis of a status page and shallow checks, and the error-rate onset is not tied to the deploy time at finer resolution. Further targeted evidence is needed before accepting the H-A conclusion.

issues.detail: The only error-level log in the window attributes a rejection to the issuer ('card declined by issuer'), and the analysis reads this as weak evidence for H-B. Payment-provider declines starting at 11:00 would produce the same onset and propagate to checkout identically, so H-B is not excluded by the data. Only payment-service error logs could separate them, and those were never obtained.

The mechanism assumes a write-path failure from C09, but no error signature (exception type, SQL error, endpoint, version split) was retrieved. The P02 match is a pattern similarity only, and the schema migration status is explicitly unknown. The 0.60 confidence is not supported by direct evidence of C09-linked failures.

Onset at 11:00 is only resolved to a 5-minute bucket, and the 10:57 deploy is 3 minutes earlier. Timing alone cannot separate the deploy from an independent event at 11:00 (for example an issuer change). Confidence should be lower until the error onset is pinned to the minute or split by instance version.

The 'status page operational' check is treated as contradicting H-B. Provider status pages routinely miss partial issuer decline spikes, as the H-B assumptions themselves note, so this check carries little weight against H-B.

The payments-db flatness is supported by metrics (connections, CPU, latency, lag all flat), so H-C is weakly supported. The analysis does correctly note that no write-only failure check was run, but the data does not clearly contradict a write-only fault.

Payment-service ERROR logs (exception types, endpoints, error codes) remain the decisive missing evidence and were never retrieved because of timeouts. A narrower retrieval (single minute, specific error code or instance) should be attempted, along with a split of error rate by instance version to see whether errors track C09-deployed hosts.

analysis.response_to_critique: Accepted that H-A was overconfident: confidence reduced from 0.60 to 0.45 because no error signature or migration record was obtained and onset is only bucket-resolved. Accepted that the issuer-decline log is not weak evidence against H-B, so H-B is raised from 0.20 to 0.25 and L0212 is moved out of H-B's contradicting list. Removed the misread of the status page as contradicting H-B. Accepted that H-C is weakly supported and lowered it to 0.10. Accepted that the missing payment-service error logs are the decisive gap and listed them first in evidence_needed. The timing and log-retrieval tasks were not re-run because the tool budget is exhausted.

critique.summary: The leading hypothesis H-A (C09 deploy causing payment write failures) is plausible on timing but rests on an unverified schema migration status and no payment-service error signature. Evidence for H-A is largely temporal. The analysis overstates H-A at 0.45 given no error logs, and H-B (issuer/provider decline) is not ruled out, since the only checkout error log is an issuer decline and provider telemetry is absent. H-A's contradicting evidence (L0212) is misread as a weak point rather than weighed, and the health checks are shallow and taken at 11:28Z, so they do not refute H-A. No further investigation is possible, so the conclusion must be revised to reflect uncertainty.

issues.detail: Confidence 0.45 is based on timing alone (only change before onset) plus a past pattern (P02). Schema migration status is unknown and no payment-service error signature was retrieved, so the mechanism is unverified. Confidence should be lower and the report should say the cause is unconfirmed.

The checkout log L0212 attributes a rejection to 'card declined by issuer'. Under H-A, payment writes fail with ORM/schema errors, which would not produce issuer declines. The analysis lists L0212 as contradicting but does not explain why a single issuer decline is outweighed, and it treats the log as a weak point rather than evidence that some failures are provider-side.

The claim that health checks do not exercise the payment write path is correct, but the report uses this to keep H-A alive without any positive evidence of a write-path failure. The 11:28Z health checks are taken after onset and are uninformative about write errors, so they neither support nor refute H-A.

Provider or issuer decline spike starting at 11:00 fits the step-change onset, the flat resource metrics, and the issuer-decline log equally well. Provider telemetry is absent, so H-B cannot be excluded and is at least as consistent as H-A. The 0.25 confidence for H-B is not justified by the evidence against it (M32/M34 flat metrics do not contradict a provider-side cause).

The report says the ORM upgrade and new idempotency_key writes could cause failures, but the change record says only that the schema migration was 'run separately', not that it was skipped. Treating the migration as possibly unapplied is an assumption, not evidence.

Payments-db metrics are flat and its health was checked by SELECT 1 only; the hypothesis is weak and appropriately low confidence, but the 0.10 rating should note that write-only failures remain untested.

Per-version or per-host error split (which would discriminate C09 hosts from all hosts) and payment-service ERROR logs remain unretrieved. This evidence was not obtained within the budget, so the final report must state that the cause is unresolved and that the leading hypothesis is not confirmed.
